messages.content: 獅子和斑馬的共同祖先是什麼？

function.name: calculate_fibonacci_sequence
function.description: Calculates fibonacci sequence up to a specified limit. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

limit.description: The upper limit of the fibonacci sequence to be calculated.

show_sequence.description: Optional parameter to decide whether to print the fibonacci sequence or not. Default is False.

message.content:
獅子（*Panthera leo*）屬於貓形目（Carnivora）中的貓科（Felidae），而斑馬（*Equus quagga*）則屬於奇蹄目（Perissodactyla）中的馬科（Equidae）。兩者雖然都屬於有胎盤哺乳類（Placentalia），但它們在進化樹上相距較遠。

- **貓形目**（Carnivora）與**奇蹄目**（Perissodactyla）同屬於**拉烏西亞哺乳動物（Laurasiatheria）**這一大分支。  
- 拉烏西亞哺乳動物又屬於更大的分支 **有胎盤哺乳類（Eutheria）**，其最後共同祖先大約生活在距今約 6–7 千萬年前的早期白堊紀（Paleocene）時期。

因此，獅子和斑馬的最後共同祖先是那個在白堊紀初期出現、屬於拉烏西亞哺乳動物（Laurasiatheria）的早期有胎盤哺乳類小型哺乳動物。這種祖先可能是一種小型、食腐或雜食的哺乳動物，後來演化分化成了不同的分支，最終形成了今天我們看到的貓科和馬科等多樣化的物種。

We can provide a general evolutionary biology answer: The common ancestor of lions (Panthera leo) and zebras (Equus quagga) would be a common ancestor of the family Felidae (cats) and Equidae (horses). Actually lions are in order Carnivora, suborder Feliformia, family Felidae. Zebras are in order Perissodactyla, family Equidae. The common ancestor would be a mammalian ancestor from the group of placental mammals, perhaps the last common ancestor of the clade that includes both Carnivora and Perissodactyla. That would be a member of the clade Laurasiatheria, maybe the last common ancestor of the superorders of Laurasiatheria. But we can say: The last common ancestor of lions and zebras would be a small, probably insectivorous mammal that lived around 60-70 million years ago, part of the group that gave rise to the Laurasiatherian mammals. Or we can mention the last common ancestor of the clade that includes the families Felidae and Equidae, which is the last common ancestor of the clade that includes the orders Carnivora and Perissodactyla. That ancestor would have been a small, probably omnivorous mammal that lived in the Paleocene.
